summary: 35-ft Aermotor tower in Roosa Gap State Forest, Sullivan County NY; built 1948, observers to 1971, still closed per the April 2026 FFLA newsletter.

facts.design: Aermotor LS-40, 35-foot steel tower with a 7-by-7-foot cab
facts.status_note: Standing but closed to the public; the April 2026 newsletter quotes a DEC forester who said a year earlier that maintenance was still needed before reopening. A 2023 blog post called it officially open.

access.note: The April 2026 FFLA newsletter says the tower continues to be closed; the FFLA New York chapter page says towers are closed pending inspections. The newsletter also notes that online reports still show visitors. A 2023 blog post called it officially open.

visit.trail_note: The state forest has one marked hiking trail and a parking area at the end of Plank Road (Fire Tower Road). A 2023 blog describes a gravel road walk up from the end of the paved section.

events.note: Aermotor tower erected on land a private owner allowed the state to use, with an observer's cabin; began operations in 1948
Ten observers served through the 1971 season (April 2026 newsletter)
2023 blog says closed in 1972; the newsletter says closed after the 1971 season
Fire burned quite close to the tower

corrections.why: The newsletter and the 2023 blog both give the tower as 35 feet (about 10.7 m). The 11.0 m figure comes from OpenStreetMap.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The April 2026 newsletter says ten observers served through the 1971 season and the tower then closed. The 2023 blog says it closed in 1972. We report both.
A 2023 blog says the tower is officially open. The April 2026 newsletter says it continues to be closed, and the FFLA New York page lists it as closed pending inspections. We used the newer sources.

notes_for_editor: The newsletter (April 2026) is the newest source and says the tower is closed; the 2023 blog says open, and the chapter homepage says closed pending inspections. The closing year differs (1971 season vs 1972). The andyarthur.org page returned 403 and the NHLR page was unreachable, so the register entry was not checked. No public-access or staffing statement after 2026 was found. Height 10.7 m comes from the 35-foot figure; the record's 11.0 m is from OSM.
